title: tm.assert_index_equal does not compare freq; assert it explicitly in tests
answers: test passes but freq is wrong
how to test that the DatetimeIndex freq is preserved
body:
Convention: tm.assert_index_equal does not check the .freq of a DatetimeIndex or TimedeltaIndex. Tests that care about freq add a separate `assert result.freq == expected.freq`, with the comment "# Not checked by assert_index_equal".
Examples: pandas/tests/reshape/concat/test_datetimes.py:TestDatetimeConcat.test_concat_datetimeindex_freq_order_independent and pandas/tests/frame/test_constructors.py:TestDataFrameConstructors.test_constructor_dict_of_series_datetimeindex_freq.
To build an expected index that must have freq=None (e.g. a non-monotonic append), use idx._with_freq(None).
When the concat test omits sort and all inputs are DatetimeIndex, wrap the call in tm.assert_produces_warning(Pandas4Warning, match="Sorting by default when concatenating all DatetimeIndex"). TimedeltaIndex inputs do not raise this warning.
